summary: Splits an array into consecutive groups of a fixed size, validating both arguments.
description:
`chunk` walks the array once and slices it into groups of `size` elements. When the length does not divide evenly,
the final group holds the remainder and is shorter than the rest. The input array is never modified.

Both arguments are validated before any work happens: a non-array input or a fractional `size` throws instead of
returning a quietly wrong result. A `size` of `0` or less, and an empty input, both produce `[]` rather than a group
of empty groups.

params.array: The array to split. Left untouched.
params.size: The length of each group. An integer; defaults to `1`.

returns: a new array of groups. Every group but the last has exactly `size` elements.

examples.title: Writing a large range in batches
Edge cases
examples.body:
```javascript
chunk([1, 2, 3]); // => [[1], [2], [3]] — size defaults to 1
chunk([], 2); // => []
chunk([1, 2, 3], 0); // => []
chunk("a,b,c", 2); // throws TypeError: Input 'array' must be an array.
chunk([1, 2, 3], 1.5); // throws TypeError: Input 'size' must be an integer.
```
